tests.requirement: Cross-sectional area of other wiring in MAINS PART and sizes of tracks on printed wiring circuits sufficient to prevent fire in case of fault currents

ME EQUIPMENT connected to SUPPLY MAINS with max available short-circuit fault, and subsequent simulation of a fault in single insulation in MAINS PART did not result in any HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS in 13.1.2
PROTECTION AGAINST MECHANICAL HAZARDS OF ME EQUIPMENT AND ME SYSTEMS
ME EQUIPMENT complies with Clause 4 for design and manufacture, and mechanical strength (15.3)
HAZARDS associated with moving parts
When ME EQUIPMENT with moving parts PROPERLY INSTALLED, used per ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTS or under foreseeable misuse, RISKS associated with moving parts reduced to an acceptable level
RISK from contact with moving parts reduced to an acceptable level using protective measures (access, function, shape of parts, energy, speed of motion, and benefits to PATIENT considered)
RESIDUAL RISK associated with moving parts considered acceptable when exposure was needed for ME EQUIPMENT to perform its intended function
RISK CONTROLS implemented
TRAPPING ZONE
ME EQUIPMENT with a TRAPPING ZONE complied with one or more: Gaps in 9.2.2.2, Safe distances in 9.2.2.3, GUARDS and other RISK CONTROL measures in 9.2.2.4, or Continuous activation in 9.2.2.5
Control of relevant motion complied with 9.2.2.6 when implementation of above protective measures were inconsistent with INTENDED USE
A TRAPPING ZONE considered not to present a MECHANICAL HAZARD when gaps of TRAPPING ZONE complied with dimensions per Table 20
A TRAPPING ZONE considered not to present a MECHANICAL HAZARD when distances separating OPERATOR, PATIENT, and others from TRAPPING ZONES exceeded values in ISO 13857:2008
Distances measured from expected positions of OPERATOR, PATIENT, and others near EQUIPMENT in NORMAL USE or under foreseeable misuse
GUARDS and other RISK CONTROL measures

A TRAPPING ZONE considered not to present a MECHANICAL HAZARD when GUARDS or other RISK CONTROL measures are of robust construction, not easy to bypass or render non-operational, and did not introduce additional unacceptable RISK based on applicable tests in 15.3 for ENCLOSURES
FIXED GUARDS held in place by systems that can only be dismantled with a TOOL

Movable GUARDS that can be opened without a TOOL remained attached when GUARD was open; associated with interlock preventing moving parts from starting while TRAPPING ZONE is accessible, stops movement when GUARD is opened; absence or failure of component prevents starting, and stops moving parts; complied with applicable tests

Other RISK CONTROL designed and incorporated into control system stops movement if a TRAPPING ZONE is reached and motion has started; SINGLE FAULT CONDITIONS have a second RISK CONTROL, or ME EQUIPMENT is SINGLE FAULT SAFE

Continuous activation used as RISK CONTROL where impractical to make TRAPPING ZONE inaccessible: a) movement in OPERATOR'S field of view; b) movement possible only by continuous activation of control; c) second RISK CONTROL provided for SINGLE FAULT CONDITION of continuous activation system

semantic_fragments.content: Clause 9 covers PROTECTION AGAINST MECHANICAL HAZARDS OF ME EQUIPMENT AND ME SYSTEMS. The device under test has no moving parts and no trapping zones, resulting in all sub-clauses under 9.2 (moving parts hazards) and 9.2.2 (trapping zones) being marked N/A. Overall verdict for Clause 9 is Pass (P) based on Clause 9.1 compliance referencing mechanical strength tests 15.3.2, 15.3.3, 15.3.4, 15.3.6.
